label: copy phase (all steps after the first copy output)
explanation: Fires on nearly every copy-phase step (t > L; 94% of them are active) and essentially nowhere else: about 0 on the original-token phase and 0.3% on the <DEL> step. It does not fire at t = L (recall_idx 0), the step that outputs the first original token. It is token-agnostic: rates by in_tok, out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, n_digits and L are all flat. Magnitude is largest on the first copy step (recall_idx 1, the input right after <DEL>), which holds about 26% of activation mass on about 18% of active steps, and generally drops over the next few copy steps. The top examples often have h among the first few original tokens, but I did not test this. The few misses are tiny activations at the last original token or at <DEL>, together 0.0% of mass. False positives are scattered copy steps with zero activation, mostly mid- to late-copy.

issues: Main claims check out. On the test split, phase == 2 gives P 0.939, R 0.999, F1 0.968, mass recall 1.0. On dev, the original phase has 943 active steps out of 3.23M with 0.000 of the mass, and the <DEL> step (t = L, recall_idx 0) fires 0.3% of the time with 0.000 of the mass.

Misses on the test split are tiny activations (about 0.02-0.13 of max) at <DEL> or at the last original token of long sequences (orig_idx 7-8, L = 8-9). Together they hold 0.0% of the mass, so they are noise.

The claim that rates are token-agnostic holds. Copy-phase precision for each in_tok value (all 30 tokens) ranges from 0.906 to 0.975. Precision is also flat for repeated vs. unique tokens (in_count > 1: 0.932, in_count == 1: 0.940).

Minor gap: the claim that rates are flat across L is slightly off. For L = 3 the copy-phase precision is only about 0.76 at recall_idx 1 and 2 (about 26k steps, about 1% of copy steps), compared with about 0.95 for L = 4. Mid-copy steps far from the end (recall_idx >= 3 and L - recall_idx >= 4) have precision 0.897. These are small rate differences, not a separate class of counterexamples.

The magnitude claim is confirmed: recall_idx 1 holds 25.7% of the mass on 18.3% of active steps, and the top examples decay over the following copy steps. The top examples often have 'h' at original positions 1-2. The explanation admits it did not test this; it is a magnitude detail and does not affect the binary predicate.
The label matches the predicate: 'all steps after the first copy output' is t > L, i.e. phase == 2.
